citation.authors: Simonis-Bik AM, Boomsma DI, Dekker JM, Diamant M, et al.
citation.title: The heritability of beta cell function parameters in a mixed meal test design

population.description: 183 healthy Dutch twins and same-sex siblings of European origin (77 men, 106 women), recruited from the Netherlands Twin Register; diabetes excluded by a 75 g OGTT in the weeks before the test. Age and BMI are the total-column means and SDs of Table 1 (text gives the age range 20 to 49 y, not taken as observed min/max). Pooled arms are not entered: the men's and women's meals differ, so the sexes are two arms with their own n.

protocols.name: men_meal
protocols.description: Men (n = 77): 3024 kJ meal (110 g brown bread, 20 g margarine, 25 g cheese, 30 g jam, 19 g honey cake, 200 ml semi-skimmed milk; printed 89 g carbohydrate, 30 g fat, 24.4 g protein). Mixed meal after a 12 h fast; procedure started at 08:00; meal eaten between paper t = 0 and 10 min; water only during the test; subjects confined to bed. Arm minute 30 = paper t = 0 (meal). The 30 min run-in before it is assumed (the paper says only that baseline samples were taken twice before the meal); pre-meal baseline = arm minutes 0 to 30. Samples at paper t = 10 to 240 min = arm minutes 40 to 270.

meals.food: brown bread, margarine, cheese, jam, honey cake and semi-skimmed milk

protocols.name: women_meal
protocols.description: Women (n = 106): the same meal at 79% of the men's, printed as 2,392 kJ, 71 g carbohydrate, 23 g fat, 19.4 g protein. Mixed meal after a 12 h fast; procedure started at 08:00; meal eaten between paper t = 0 and 10 min; water only during the test; subjects confined to bed. Arm minute 30 = paper t = 0 (meal). The 30 min run-in before it is assumed (the paper says only that baseline samples were taken twice before the meal); pre-meal baseline = arm minutes 0 to 30. Samples at paper t = 10 to 240 min = arm minutes 40 to 270.

left_out.what: all Table 1 'Total' (both sexes, n = 183) values of the entered families: fasting insulin, insulin at t120, insulin IAUC, glucose at t120, glucose t30 minus t0, glucose IAUC 0-120 and 0-240; the two sexes had different meals (men 3024 kJ, women 79% of it), so no one arm holds the pooled group

serum insulin at t120 (Table 1: men 19.9 +/- 13.0, women 21.2 +/- 11.8 pmol/l; total 20.7), printed below the fasting values (33.9, 35.4) although glucose at t120 (5.29, 5.46 mmol/l) is above the paper's own approximate fasting glucose of 4.5 mmol/l and the incremental ISR over 30-120 min is positive; the row cannot be reconciled with the rest of the table, so it is not entered
glucose and insulin at each sampling time (paper t = 10 to 240 min; the time course between t120 and t240 in particular): not printed in text or tables; Table 1 gives only t0, t30, t120 and the areas
